report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food-preparation domain (cooking, baking, restaurants, chefs), with a “professional kitchen” flavor.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary,” “baking,” “Cooking,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Restaurant,” “Chef,” “Cake,” “Baked/Bake,” “flavor,” “citrus,” and repeatedly “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This pattern is consistent across many layers (14–25) and positions (p1–p4), not just a few outliers.
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (peaking ~L20–L25), which is where high-level semantic features typically live, supporting that this is a semantic domain shift rather than a surface artifact.
- Early-layer hints (“photographic,” “excellence,” “innovation,” “dissertation”) are less consistent; the later layers converge strongly on culinary vocabulary.
- Patchscope readouts were not provided, but the logit-lens signal is strong and coherent enough to support the domain inference.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B appears fine-tuned or biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant/professional-kitchen content. I cannot identify a more specific objective beyond this domain shift from the evidence given.
